$description: Struct-level golden vectors for postFieldBytes — the post id and PoW preimage (TYPES_INTERFACE -> Layout - Post). RESET at Phase 2: these bytes are the positional dialect, not the fixed-width-LE one, and every post id in the system moved with them. The encode direction runs the production writer; the decode direction runs an independent reader written from the layout table, so a vector also proves the preimage is self-delimiting and canonical.

vectors.name: post/minimal
vectors.note: 68 bytes: 1 + 0 content, 32 author, 1 count, 32 challenge, 1 version, 1 timestamp. The struct's own shape, with every field at its zero value — so the byte COUNT is what this pins, and nothing else can. Content and protocolVersion sit below their protocol minimums (1 byte; PROTOCOL_VERSION is 1): the encoder has no floor, and the domain is upstream of it.

vectors.name: post/golden
vectors.note: 132 bytes, and THE cross-implementation anchor: the demo UI's hand-written mirror is asserted byte-identical to it. Adjacent fields hold distinct non-zero values (author 00..1f, ref 11.., challenge 20..3f), because an all-zeros vector cannot detect a field-order swap and field order IS the specification. One parent ref, not two: MAX_PARENT_REFS is 1.

vectors.name: post/no-refs
vectors.note: post/golden with the ref removed: exactly 32 bytes shorter. That delta is the dialect change with the largest byte impact — a ref used to cost u32LE(64) + the 64 characters of its hex TEXT, 68 bytes, and now costs the 32 raw bytes it names.

vectors.name: post/wide-numerics
vectors.note: Both vlqU fields at MAX_SAFE_INTEGER — eight bytes each, the top of the encodable number domain. One byte more and readVlqU raises vlq-overflow, which is exactly what keeps the ten-byte all-ones sentinel from ever decoding back into a plausible value.

vectors.name: post/multibyte-content
vectors.note: lpUtf8 counts BYTES, not characters: 11 characters encode as 0x12 = 18 bytes. Two refs so the array's count byte is not stuck at 0 or 1 (the ENCODER has no cap — MAX_PARENT_REFS is a validation rule, and putting it inside the writer would be a guard added to compensate for a domain, which the format forbids). timestamp 128 is the two-byte VLQ boundary.

vectors.name: powNonceTail/zero
vectors.note: ONE byte. A fixed-width u64 tail spends eight here, so the two dialects differ at nonce 0 as much as anywhere — and 0 is where a test asserting only 'the id moved when the nonce moved' still passes under either. That is the shape of the split this vector exists to close.

vectors.name: powNonceTail/128-first-two-byte
vectors.note: The width boundary: the tail grows with the nonce instead of being eight bytes always, so a mined post's id depends on how long mining took.

vectors.name: powNonceTail/typical-mined
vectors.note: Protocol-typical: POST_POW_TARGET_BITS is 20, so a post is mined at roughly 2^20 hashes and its tail is three bytes.

vectors.name: powNonceTail/max-safe-integer
vectors.note: 2^53-1 — the largest in-domain nonce, and the same bound on both sides: it is the top of `vlqU`'s encodable domain AND of `isU64Safe`, the guard in `@dagsocial/validation` that keeps the sentinel below unreachable from `verifyPoW`.

vectors.name: powNonceTail/sentinel-out-of-domain
vectors.note: The tail is TOTAL: a negative nonce sentinels rather than throwing, so -1, NaN, 1.5 and 2^60 share these bytes and therefore one postId. Pinned on the export because that collision must stay closed upstream — adding a domain check inside this writer would break the no-panic contract (TYPES_INTERFACE → Canonical field encoding). primitives.json's `vlqU/sentinel-*` group pins the same bytes for the primitive.

vectors.name: powPreimage/nonce-zero
vectors.note: 133 bytes: post/golden's 132, then the tail. THE byte string the PoW hash covers — `computePostId` domain-tags it, `verifyPoW` hashes it bare, and the demo UI's solvePoW builds it per candidate nonce. The three producers agree here or they do not agree at all.

vectors.name: powPreimage/nonce-typical-mined
vectors.note: 135 bytes. Same fields as nonce-zero, so the diff against it is exactly the tail — which is what makes the boundary between preimage and tail reviewable rather than merely asserted.

vectors.name: powPreimage/nonce-max-safe-integer
vectors.note: 140 bytes — the widest a well-formed preimage gets. Eight tail bytes, so the encoding coincides with the fixed-width one in LENGTH exactly once, at the top of the domain, and in VALUE not even there.

rejects.name: powNonceTail/non-minimal-zero
rejects.note: Nonce 0 written with one byte of VLQ padding. It decodes to 0, so only the re-encode compare separates it from `00` — the step that makes the tail canonical rather than merely parseable, and the reason a second writer emitting padded bytes is a defect and not a variant.

rejects.name: post/non-minimal-content-length
rejects.note: post/minimal with the content length written as the padded `80 00` instead of `00`. Decodes to a byte-identical value, so steps 1 and 2 both pass and only the re-encode compare separates it.

rejects.name: post/trailing-byte
rejects.note: post/minimal with one byte appended. The struct is fully satisfied before the input runs out — step 2.

rejects.name: post/truncated-author
rejects.note: Empty content and then 19 of the author's 32 bytes. Wire's own rejection, not a boundary-check one: a fixed-width read that runs off the end.

rejects.name: post/timestamp-past-safe-integer
rejects.note: The timestamp written as u64-max — the ten bytes a malformed number field takes on the ENCODE side. It must not decode back into anything, which is the property that makes the sentinel unreachable from a well-formed post rather than merely unlikely.
